key_insights: Recommends preparing to talk about oneself across academic, extracurricular, and family/personal life areas, since interviewers may explore any of these.

Advises coming prepared with school-specific, personal questions for the interviewer (e.g., about a professor, program, or the interviewer's own experience) rather than questions easily answered by a guidebook.
States that if a student mentions a specific interest or topic, the interviewer may follow up in depth on it, so students should only bring up subjects they can actually discuss further.

Notes that at some colleges the interview has a secondary purpose of gauging demonstrated interest, and skipping a strongly encouraged or required interview (especially for students living within a couple hours of campus) may be read as lower interest.
Suggests students unable to attend an in-person interview for reasons like distance or scheduling should proactively contact the school to arrange an alternative such as a phone or video interview.

Frames the ideal interview tone as conversational rather than interrogative, with interviewers described as generally 'chatty' people genuinely trying to get to know the applicant, not trying to catch them out.
